This would lock up the cache if the status is `THREAD_LOAD_INVALID_RESOURCE` or `THREAD_LOAD_FAILED`. You should return if the status is `THREAD_LOAD_IN_PROGRESS`. And handle the error statuses after setting `is_loading` to `false`.

I personally don't think that we should hide this loading logic behind this editor setting which AFAIK is off by default.

The setting is about running the Language server on a separate thread then the editor to prevent stalling, however there have been issues reported with it like random crashes when saving files. Loading scenes on a different thread comes with no negative side effects so I don't think we need to have an option for it.

body:
What I meant with an DEBUG_LSP macro wasn't like a print macro, but an optional definition to enable LSP logging. Having the server this verbose in all dev builds will just spam developers who are working on something else.

```cpp
// #define DEBUG_LSP

...

#ifdef DEBUG_LSP
// do verbose logging
#endif
```

Specifically those logs should not be enabled by default in dev builds. When working on the language server one can simply uncomment the definition.

E.g. the xml parser does it like this: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3c7f9b937214068bc892be0d2bd9a8a7026edae1/core/io/xml_parser.cpp#L35
This is an opaque cache. Exposing `has` makes no sense. (Except for testing purposes, but as far as I looked into it, this class can't really be tested since we can't really mock `EditorFileSystem`)
Those methods are called twice at most. Please just do the uri -> path conversion on the call side. The methods add another singleton dependency to the class, I'd like to keep such dependencies low.

This code does look wrong to me. I can't really test it since vscode always sends those openDocument signals way in advance, but some things to note:

- This code crashes with an empty resource queue, this can happen when the client did not send an open notification. This would be a client bug, but we should not crash because of it.
- It replaces the head of the request queue, this seems to work at the moment, but I'm very worried that it might lead to some invalid state in some edge case.
- The while loop at the end would get stuck if loading failed for some reason. This makes graceful error handling using the error macros very dangerous. While you don't use those at the moment, the regression potential is way to high IMO.
